title: Kestrel Auto Refill & Medication Sync Terms of Enrollment
content:
Enrolling a prescription in an Auto Refill & Medication Sync program is the patient's own consent to automated refills, and it is done by the patient. Each enrollment is one prescription in one program. The following terms decide whether a prescription may be enrolled in a given program; each is read from Kestrel's records as they stand at the time of enrollment, for the very prescription being enrolled and the patient enrolling it, and a statement by the patient does not take the place of the record.

## Terms

**1. Consent.** Enrolling is the patient's own consent to automated refills and is done by the patient.

**2. Prescription status and class.** A prescription is enrolled only while its Prescriptions record shows it in received or active status and its handling class has set to true the Prescriptions charter eligibility switch named for the program — Auto Refill eligible, Med Sync eligible or adherence packaging eligible.

**3. 90-day supply.** Where the program requires it, the prescription's class must allow a 90-day supply.

**4. Prior fills.** The prescription must have at least the program's required number of dispensed fills at Kestrel.

**5. Delivery plan.** A program that requires a delivery plan is enrolled only while the patient holds a delivery plan under Delivery & Pickup Services in enrolled or active status, as the patient's own delivery plan record shows it.

**6. Fulfilment method.** The fulfilment method chosen for the enrollment must be one of the methods the program offers.

**7. Re-enrollment after the program ends an enrollment.** A prescription whose enrollment was ended by the program (an enrollment in ended status, as distinct from one the patient stopped) is not enrolled again before its closing date plus the re-enrollment wait, a number of calendar days set per program. The clock starts on the closing date recorded on the ended enrollment and runs in calendar days; the earliest day on which the prescription may be enrolled again is the closing date plus the wait, that is, for a wait of 30 days, the thirtieth calendar day after the closing date. An enrollment on that day meets this term; an enrollment on any earlier day does not.

**8. Annual consent.** Where the program requires consent to be renewed every program year, the patient renews the enrollment at each program-year anniversary, or the enrollment ends as consent not renewed. A program year begins on the enrollment date, and each anniversary of it begins the next program year.

**9. Fee.** Enrollment costs the program's enrollment fee.

## Checklist form of terms 2 to 6

| Term | Record read | Met when |
|---|---|---|
| Status | The prescription's Prescriptions record | Received or active |
| Class switch | The prescription's handling class | The switch named for the program is true |
| 90-day supply | The prescription's handling class | Allowed, where the program requires it |
| Prior fills | The prescription's dispensed fills at Kestrel | At least the program's required number |
| Delivery plan | The patient's delivery plan under Delivery & Pickup Services | Enrolled or active, where the program requires a plan |
| Fulfilment method | The method chosen for this enrollment | One the program offers |

## Boundary dates for term 7 (hypothetical)

Hypothetical inputs: the program ended an enrollment with a closing date of 10 March, and the program's re-enrollment wait is taken as 30 calendar days.

- 10 March plus 30 calendar days is 9 April (21 days to the end of March, then 9 days into April).
- An enrollment of the same prescription on 9 April meets term 7.
- An enrollment of the same prescription on 8 April falls before the closing date plus the wait and does not.

## After enrollment

A new enrollment begins in enrolled status and becomes active when its first automated cycle is scheduled.
